Hesabın sunucuda kullanabileceği işlemci: The processor and memory the account may use on the server. A field left empty means unlimited.
Kullanım, hesabın SSH oturumları, zamanl: Usage is the total of the account's SSH sessions, scheduled tasks and (once the limit applies) its Redis and applications; it appears empty while the account runs no active process.
Node.js ve Python uygulamaları ile hesab: Node.js and Python applications and the account's Redis join the account's total limit the next time they are restarted after the limit changes.
PHP sitelerinde memory_limit değeri pake: On PHP sites the memory_limit value cannot exceed the package's memory limit; if it does, it is lowered to the limit.
Bir çekirdeğin yüzdesi: 100 = bir tam çe: Percent of one core: 100 = one full core, 250 = two and a half cores.
Hesabın bütün süreçlerinin (SSH, zamanlı: Total limit for all of the account's processes (SSH, scheduled tasks, Redis). On PHP sites each process's memory_limit is clamped to this limit.
Bir sitenin aynı anda çalıştırabileceği: The most PHP processes a site can run at the same time (pm.max_children).
Hesabın en çok kaç süreç ve iş parçacığı: The most processes and threads the account can run.
Bu sunucuda işlemci ve bellek sınırları: CPU and memory limits cannot be applied on this server.
Bu sunucuda cgroup v2 yok; sınırlar kayd: This server has no cgroup v2; the limits were saved but cannot be applied.
Bu sunucuda işlemci denetleyicisi kullan: The CPU controller is not delegated to user slices on this server (this can happen in an unprivileged container); the limits were saved but cannot be applied.
Bu sunucuda bellek denetleyicisi kullanı: The memory controller is not delegated to user slices on this server (this can happen in an unprivileged container); the limits were saved but cannot be applied.
Bu sunucuda işlemci ve bellek denetleyic: The CPU and memory controllers are not delegated to user slices on this server (this can happen in an unprivileged container); the limits were saved but cannot be applied.
